dedupe_keys.name: unctad sidsport climateadapt climate impacts and adaptation for seaports and airports in jamaica and saint lucia

description: SIDSport-ClimateAdapt is the web platform of a UN Development Account project (UNDA 1415O), led by UNCTAD with UNECLAC, UNDP, UNEP, the Caribbean Community Climate Change Centre, the OECS Commission, the European Commission Joint Research Centre and academic experts, on climate change impacts on coastal transport infrastructure in Caribbean small island developing states. The project built national case studies of Jamaica and Saint Lucia that assess potential climate impacts on each country's main seaports and airports and the options for adaptation, together with a transferable methodology for assessing climate-related impacts and adaptation options for coastal transport infrastructure in SIDS. The Saint Lucia page notes that its airports, seaports and fuel storage all lie on the coast or on low-lying reclaimed land, that average yearly losses from hydro-meteorological events in 1992 to 2011 were about 2% of GDP, and that Hurricane Tomas in 2010 caused losses of 336.2 million US dollars (43.4% of GDP). The Jamaica report reviews the island's climate, trends and projections before assessing its facilities. Results were discussed at national workshops and a regional workshop in Barbados. Coverage: Jamaica and Saint Lucia. Access: free web pages and reports. Licence and cost: UN publication, free. Caveats: the project dates from the late 2010s and the analyses are not updated. It informs climate adaptation, hazard exposure and resilience planning of island ports and airports. It relates to the Jamaica infrastructure risk assessment platform, the NISMOD-LP Saint Lucia model and the global port multi-hazard risk data in the catalogue.
